BACKPORT: FROMGIT: platform/chrome: wilco_ec: Add event handling The Wilco Embedded Controller can create custom events that are not handled as standard ACPI objects. These events can contain information about changes in EC controlled features, such as errors and events in the dock or display. For example, an event is triggered if the dock is plugged into a display incorrectly. These events are needed for telemetry and diagnostics reasons, and for possibly alerting the user. These events are triggered by the EC with an ACPI Notify(0x90), and then the BIOS reads the event buffer from EC RAM via an ACPI method. When the OS receives these events via ACPI, it passes them along to this driver. The events are put into a queue which can be read by a userspace daemon via a char device that implements read() and poll(). The event queue acts as a circular buffer of size 64, so if there are no userspace consumers the kernel will not run out of memory. The char device will appear at /dev/wilco_event{n}, where n is some small non-negative integer, starting from 0. Standard ACPI events such as the battery getting plugged/unplugged can also come through this path, but they are dealt with via other paths, and are ignored here. To test, you can tail the binary data with $ cat /dev/wilco_event0 | hexdump -ve '1/1 "%x\n"' and then create an event by plugging/unplugging the battery. Signed-off-by: Nick Crews <ncrews@chromium.org> (cherry picked from commit f7b0bc5eafa44941ddf92df6f46dd82cbfacec3e git://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/chrome-platform/linux.git chrome-platform-5.3) [ncrews: This CL updates the previous chromium version so it cleanly reflects the v4 version sent to the mailing list.] BUG=b:133444996 TEST=See the commit message for instructions. Only 64 events are available to read, even if I generate more than 64 of them. Cq-Depend: chromium:1628140, chromium:1628141, chromium:1628142, chromium:1628143 Change-Id: I1d9feaa4d83f18011320bc8c35620504adf70f9d Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1628144 Tested-by: Nick Crews <ncrews@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Nick Crews <ncrews@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Daniel Kurtz <djkurtz@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: hardlockup: detect hard lockups without NMIs using secondary cpus Emulate NMIs on systems where they are not available by using timer interrupts on other cpus. Each cpu will use its softlockup hrtimer to check that the next cpu is processing hrtimer interrupts by verifying that a counter is increasing. This patch is useful on systems where the hardlockup detector is not available due to a lack of NMIs, for example most ARM SoCs. Without this patch any cpu stuck with interrupts disabled can cause a hardware watchdog reset with no debugging information, but with this patch the kernel can detect the lockup and panic, which can result in useful debugging info. FROMGIT: mwifiex: Fix possible buffer overflows at parsing bss descriptor mwifiex_update_bss_desc_with_ie() calls memcpy() unconditionally in a couple places without checking the destination size. Since the source is given from user-space, this may trigger a heap buffer overflow. Fix it by putting the length check before performing memcpy(). This fix addresses CVE-2019-3846. shill: connection: Use per-device tables for all connections This change causes Connection to use a per-device table for all connections, and sets up routing rules such that the routing behavior complies with Shill's priority rules. In particular, VPNs must be used when applicable, and priorities of physical interfaces should follow Shill's Service sorting order. This implementation, as with the previous routing setup, does not adequately handle the case where two distinct interfaces have the same subnet. Future changes that allow for socket marking and routing based on packet marks will be needed to resolve this issue. Note that there is an existing issue (crbug.com/938629) where a non-default physical interface is used for all v4 or v6 traffic when the default physical interface does not have connectivity for that IP version. This CL does not change the existing behavior with respect to that issue. mist: clean up using statements Platform C++ code conventionally uses using std::*, base::* statements to make code more concise. The readability gain is arguably marginal. Unfortunately, as the code base evolves, it has mixed use of using statements and fully qualified names. To remove the inconsistency and reduce the mental load on when to use using statements, this CL removes most of the using statements, except those testing::*, in the code base. Keeping testing::* using statements are generally recommended to make test code more readable. BUG=None TEST=Run unit tests. tast-tests: Skip hwsec.ChallengeResponseMount w/o TPM Add a dependency on the "tpm" feature into the hwsec.ChallengeResponseMount, so that the test is skipped when running on a system without the TPM chip functionality. The functionality that the test verifies - the challenge-response mount - heavily relies on the TPM, so the test cannot work without it. This change should, in particular, suppress the spurious failures of this test on the "betty" board (which is a VM without the TPM emulation).
